item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is closer to the frozen contract because it preserves the existing lower-level Add behavior while adding the requested replayable multipart convenience API. B has better integration tests, but materially and unnecessarily changes Add by eagerly buffering every caller-supplied body.","reasons":["A explicitly validates empty filenames and nil content, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", and preserves FilesOption handling and response semantics.","B changes Add from a streaming lower-level API into an eager io.ReadAll operation, altering memory use, reader-error timing, and behavior for large or unbounded bodies contrary to the preservation and scope requirements.","Both patches fail the explicit requirement that Upload route through FilesService.Add: A duplicates Add's implementation, while B bypasses Add through a new private add method. A's violation is less damaging because it does not also alter Add's public behavior.","B's retry test is stronger and directly verifies multipart field, filename, content, and replay after 429, but test quality does not outweigh its public API semantic regression."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's request, option, decoding, and error logic instead of calling Add, creating a maintenance divergence point.","The Upload test does not assert uploaded content and does not cover retry, validation, or source-reader failures; the generic transport test is not an end-to-end Upload retry test.","The combined validation error is less precise than separate filename and content errors."],"risks_b":["Add now buffers all custom multipart bodies in memory and fails while pre-reading them, changing established behavior outside the requested convenience API.","Upload does not visibly perform the required filename and nil-content validation before invoking the helper.","The new private add method means Upload does not route through the existing Add method as explicitly required and introduces extra machinery primarily to support the out-of-scope Add change."]}
